bifurcation.note: DECLARED BEFORE ANY REFERENCE WAS OPENED, AND NARROWER THAN ROUND 1'S ON PURPOSE. Round 1 declared `both-separately` and then could not capture the FIDELITY half, which set the whole piece to 0 on an axis nobody had measured. This round I declare ART_DIRECTION ONLY and I did not capture FIDELITY either — so rather than carry a disjoint set I cannot populate, RI-UIX06 is scored on its ART side with the scope written into the item entry and into `notes`. Every Morrowind plate cited here is cited for arrangement, materials, iconography and populated density; no 2002-era or OpenMW capture is cited anywhere as evidence of a rendering metric, and this verdict contains no fidelity number at all. RI-UIX09 is explicitly a design property — how many drawn things, not how sharply they resolve — and its own §A says citing its plates under FIDELITY voids a verdict.

checks.observed: KEYBOARD. Every drawn affordance operated through real KeyboardEvents and moved: inventory columns (col 1->0->1), category walk (tagIdx 0->1, rows 20->7), the sort control (sortIdx 0->1 AND the list reordered), item rows with the detail panel following, the journal's page turns and quest index (indexIdx 0->1, view -> chronicle), search entry and the ring typing a character, sheet and spells row walks, the map's view swap, wait hours (1->2), the container's side switch and transfer BOTH WAYS (carried 44 -> 45 -> 44), open, close, and the whole peer ring [inventory, map, sheet, journal, spells, wait, world] with nothing skipped.

GAMEPAD. START opens; the left stick walks the item rows; D-pad LEFT moves exactly one column (1 -> 0); A confirms; START closes; button 15 walks the ring inventory -> map; an irrelevant button (GUIDE) leaves the screen stable.

TOUCH, AND IT BREAKS AT A NAMED LINK. The drawer exposes menu, swap_left and swap_right and they work — tapping touch.swap_right took the mode inventory -> map. THE FLOATING STICK DOES NOT REACH THE PIPELINE: pointerdown in the left half sets touch.stick.active true; a pointermove of +140 px sets stick.y = -1; and after four fixed steps input.moveX and input.moveY are STILL 0 and the focus has not moved. On a handheld you can open a screen and turn its pages and you cannot walk any list on it.

MOUSE. game/src/ui/system.js rule 2 declares no pointer path for these surfaces — 'a menu that needs a mouse is a menu the owner cannot use' — and §C's row passes a build that says so. A click on a row does nothing, and that is the declared design rather than a lie. The category plates ARE drawn as tabs, which implies a click; recorded as a secondary observation, not scored as a fail, because failing it would be scoring taste against a documented pad-first decision that serves the owner.

THE JOURNAL'S SEARCH VIEW HAS NO EXIT. `confirm` on the chronicle enters it. Fifteen actions tried one at a time — roll, block, parry, heavy, sprint, jump, use_item, lock_on, two_hand, crouch, spell_cycle and all four axes — and every one leaves focus.journal.view === 'search', except roll, which exits the ENTIRE SCREEN to world. `backOrSub()`, the method written for exactly this, is defined at game/src/ui/system.js:711 and is called nowhere. AND THE SCREEN PROMISES THE CONTROL IN WRITING: its own foot hint, photographed at screens/critic-journal-stuck-search__1920x1080.png, reads 'Walk the letters, confirm to add one, BACK TO REMOVE ONE. Results are in the order they happened.' Back does not remove one; back closes the journal. backOrSub()'s first branch is `if (j.query.length) { j.query = j.query.slice(0, -1); return this.mode; }` — that promise, implemented, unreachable. This is not merely a dead control; it is a control the screen has written a promise for and does not keep.

The trap is permanent for the session. Walking back to the journal returns view 'search' with the query intact ('B' in the first run, '' in the second). Neither open() nor close() resets focus.journal.

EQUIP IS SILENT. Confirm on 'Bog-iron maul', out of combat, 60 frames with the screen open: equipment ['chitin-cuirass@chest','reed-cutter@right'] unchanged, doll children unchanged, row list unchanged, detail unchanged, FRAME 5 -> 5. Close the screen, 90 frames: ['bog-iron-maul@right','chitin-cuirass@chest'], with the toast 'You put on the bog-iron maul.' The control is not dead; the screen said NOTHING at the moment of the press, for longer than O3's 15-frame window by two orders of magnitude.

INSTRUMENT HONESTY. I0 asserted (real.attached true, ArrowRight -> input.moveX 1, KeyM -> pendingPress 8192); I1 asserted (touch.enabled, touch.attached, surface hook); I2 named, measured and disarmed. Counts recorded: 44 checks across four probes, every interaction with its before and after state.

how_we_lose_hits: 'The probe reaches past the input layer' — HIT BY EVERY PRE-EXISTING INSTRUMENT. t4-r2-measure.mjs, critic-t4-lean.mjs and critic-t4-shots.mjs all drive the screens through openMenu() and uiFocus(), which is why none of them could see OP5, OP6 or OP7.

'An instrument trap is reported as a defect' — HIT BY ME, FOUR TIMES, and caught each time by re-running rather than by reasoning. The four are in method_deviations and in the status file's could_not_do, first.

'The exit walk is done by reasoning about the code instead of pressing' — NOT hit, and the item exists partly because it would have been fatal here: backOrSub() reads correctly and handles the search view exactly as it should. Only pressing fifteen buttons found that nothing calls it.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Two hard fails — a screen state with no exit, and the inventory's primary verb producing no visible change — plus a touch arm on which no list on any screen can be walked. The item caps at 2 on either hard fail alone.
reference_items.path_to_ten: 1) OP5/OP6: call `this.backOrSub()` instead of `this.back()` in UISystem.step, and reset focus.journal.view to 'chronicle' in close(). 2) OP7: draw the pending equip on the row and the doll the moment _queue({kind:'equip'}) fires, or resolve the commitment immediately out of combat, since P7's 30 committed frames exist to make you vulnerable IN a fight. 3) OP3: connect TouchInput.tick()'s pipe.setMove() to the UI driver's uiMoveX||moveX read while a menu is open, and add a --leg menu-stick arm that fails when a drag with a screen open does not move getUIState().focus.

score.band_label: min over the seven items this piece is: RI-UIX03 3, RI-UIX04 6 (10/12), RI-UIX06 4 (ART only), RI-UIX07 5, RI-UIX08 2, RI-UIX09 2, RI-UIX10 2. RI-UIX01 (§A/§B/§C measured in round 1, §D never measured in either round) is recorded and EXCLUDED with its reason, so that an unmeasured item does not set the number. The min is 2 and it is set THREE WAYS: RI-UIX08's procedural cap for an unrun §G, RI-UIX09's DN4 hard fail, and RI-UIX10's OP5 and OP7 hard fails. Two of those three are real, measured defects rather than procedure.

biggest_gap.what: One press of `confirm` on the journal's chronicle puts `focus.journal.view` into 'search', and no input in the build's own closed action set returns it. I drove all fifteen — roll, block, parry, heavy, sprint, jump, use_item, lock_on, two_hand, crouch, spell_cycle and all four movement axes — one at a time, through real DOM KeyboardEvents in mode `play-instrumented` with the input path asserted live (real.attached true, ArrowRight -> input.moveX 1). Fourteen leave `view === 'search'`; the fifteenth, `roll`, exits the entire screen to `world`. Walking back to the journal from any peer returns `view: 'search'` with the query intact, because neither `open()` nor `close()` resets `focus.journal`. The player has permanently lost the journal for the session by pressing the button the interface tells them to press. `backOrSub()` — defined at game/src/ui/system.js:711, which leaves the search view for the chronicle, then the index for the chronicle, then the screen, exactly as required — is CALLED NOWHERE in the tree. AND THE SCREEN PROMISES THE WAY OUT IN WRITING: the search view's own foot hint, photographed at corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/T4-r2c/screens/critic-journal-stuck-search__1920x1080.png, reads 'Walk the letters, confirm to add one, BACK TO REMOVE ONE. Results are in the order they happened.' Back does not remove one. Back closes the journal. backOrSub()'s first branch is exactly that promise, implemented and unreachable — which makes this not a missing feature but a broken one, and the remedy a call site rather than a design.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-UIX04 scores 11 of 12 on this same build and every one of its rows is about what the journal CONTAINS; none of them can see that the screen holding all of it can be shut in the player's face by one keystroke. That is the exact defect CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.2b was written for two days after the project shipped a dialogue window measuring ΔE 0.00 that the owner could not use, and it is the second instance of the same shape in the same week.

remedy.action: In `UISystem.step` (game/src/ui/system.js), change `if (!inCombat && input.pressedName('roll')) this.back();` to call `this.backOrSub()` — the method is already defined at line 711 and already leaves the search view for the chronicle, then the index for the chronicle, then the screen. Then reset `focus.journal.view` to 'chronicle' and `focus.journal.query` to '' inside `close()`, so a sub-view cannot survive a screen the player has shut.
remedy.acceptance: From `mode: 'journal'` with `focus.journal.view === 'search'` and a non-empty query, ONE real `roll` press removes one character; with an empty query it leaves `mode === 'journal'` with `focus.journal.view === 'chronicle'`; a further `roll` leaves the screen; and entering the journal from ANY of the peers in the walk ring returns `view: 'chronicle'`. `node tools/ui/t4-r2-critic-focus.mjs` must report JS1 and JS2 green (all 15 actions plus both axes enumerated), and the delete-the-fix arm — restore `this.back()` — must turn both red again, so the guard is proven to fail in both directions (HAZARDS §0b).

secondary_observations: THE EQUIP CONTROL IS SILENT OUT OF COMBAT, and it is this piece's second hard fail (RI-UIX10 OP7). It is not the named gap only because exactly one is permitted. `_applyUIPending()` sets `_equipCommit.at = frame + 30` and `_finishEquipCommit()` waits for `sim.frame >= at`; on a paused frame that never arrives, so the screen shows nothing until it is closed and 90 frames of world have run. Remedy: draw the pending equip on the row and on the doll the moment `_queue({kind:'equip'})` fires, or resolve the commitment immediately out of combat — P7's 30 committed frames exist to make you vulnerable IN a fight and there is no fight. Acceptance: confirm on a weapon row out of combat changes at least one declared element within 15 frames.

ON TOUCH, NO LIST ON ANY SCREEN CAN BE WALKED. The stick registers the drag (touch.stick.active true, stick.y -1) and input.moveX/moveY stay 0 through four fixed steps. Remedy: connect TouchInput.tick()'s pipe.setMove() to the UI driver's `uiMoveX || moveX` read while a menu is open — the `menuOpen` path is the first place to look — and add a `--leg menu-stick` arm to tools/touch/critic-fight.mjs that fails when a drag with a screen open does not move getUIState().focus.

`hud.place` RENDERS THE RAW CELL ID. The world capture reads `thorn-hall`, lowercase and hyphenated, where RI-UIX07 W5 asks for 'the name of the cell you just entered'. Remedy: give cells a `display_name` in game/data/world/ and read it here; acceptance is that no place_name element's text matches /^[a-z0-9-]+$/.

THE PANEL IS A FIXED 57.2% BOX ON EVERY SCREEN AND ARBITRATION S56 ALREADY RULED ON IT — not listed as the gap because the ruling IS the dispatch. The arithmetic, so the next builder has a target rather than an instruction: at the matter each screen already draws, D2 >= 0.35 is reached at 24.9% of frame for the inventory, 21.5% for the journal, 14.9% for level-up, 14.6% for the sheet and 11.5% for spells. Morrowind's inventory window is ~24% of its frame. Sizing the panel to its contents clears P4 everywhere WITH NO NEW CONTENT AT ALL.

`two_hand` (the HUD full/minimal switch) IS NOT BROKEN, AND ESTABLISHING THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING I DID FOR THE NEXT CRITIC. I recorded it as a failure three times and it was my clock every time. The fourth pass read the pipeline at four points: after stepFrames(20) with the inventory open, getFrame() is STILL 5 — the screen pauses the world out of combat (correctly; that is M-P1) and hold-gate.js's inputNow() returns frame*STEP_MS in every mode except `play`, so IN A HARNESS THE HOLD CLOCK IS THE PAUSED CLOCK AND A GATED HOLD CAN NEVER BE CROSSED WHILE A PAUSED SCREEN IS OPEN. framesHeld computes 0 against a 12-frame gate. A real player is unaffected — in mode `play` the gate reads event.timeStamp. This is now RI-UIX10 §B trap I2.

THE CATEGORY COLUMN IS DRAWN AS TAB-SHAPED PLATES, which is Morrowind-faithful (its inventory has category tabs) and is also the strongest click affordance on a screen with no pointer path. Not scored as a failure; worth a decision if a pointer path is ever added.

The min is 2 and it is set three ways — RI-UIX08's procedural cap for an unrun §G, RI-UIX09's DN4 hard fail on panel fill, and RI-UIX10's OP5 and OP7 hard fails on operability. Two of those three are measured defects; one is procedure. RI-UIX01 IS EXCLUDED FROM THE AGGREGATE for the second round running: §A/§B/§C pass and §D — the stamina bar's same-frame truth, its regen state, its contrast on the three worst backgrounds, its size and its spend timing — has never been measured by anyone, and it is the correctness half of the one element the combat model requires the player to read. That debt now has two rounds on it and should be dispatched as its own piece rather than carried by a screens critique a third time.
